newsitem.title: USA: Blue-chip stocks post biggest loss in a month.
newsitem.headline: Blue-chip stocks post biggest loss in a month.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks skidded to their biggest loss in a month Wednesday as earnings jitters grew and traders used an unfounded rumour that Russian President Boris Yeltsin had died as an excuse to take profits.
The Dow Jones industrial average ended 36.15 points lower at 5,930.62, which was the largest fall since Sept. 5, when it dropped 49.94 points.
In the broader market, declining issues beat advances 1,453 to 890 on active volume of 405 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.

"The Yeltsin rumour was just one excuse," said Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments. "The real essence of the decline was the fear of earnings and, from a technical standpoint, the market's failure over the past two days to close above 6,000."
After topping 6,000 points for the first time in intra-day trading Monday and breaching the major milestone briefly on Tuesday, the Dow did not even flirt with the level on Wednesday.
A rumour of that Yeltin had died hit financial markets in mid-morning, sparking a sell-off of nearly 50 points in the Dow.
Russian authorities quickly denied the rumours, insisting that Yeltsin was working from a sanatorium outside of Moscow, which helped shave the market's loss.
"People are leery here. We're waiting to see the parade of earnings come out," said Cardillo. "Are we waiting for a 10 percent correction? Now? Absolutely not."
Analysts said the market was also bracing for Friday's data on September producer prices and retail sales, which should shed more light on the direction of inflation and the economy.

Stocks won over yet another convert, with Morgan Stanley's Chief U.S. Equity Strategist Byron Wien changing his model U.S. equity portfolio, increasing the money allocated to stocks and decreasing cash, each by 5 percent.
Morgan Stanley said the move, which puts the portfolio at 85 percent stocks and 15 percent cash reflected a change in Wien's near-term view. Wien had been forecasting a 1,000-point fall in the Dow.

The technology-laden Nasdaq Composite index ended only modestly lower, off 2.17 points at 1,237.98 as most chip stocks rose on a bullish September book-to-bill report, which is a measure of the semiconductor industry's activity.
Computer-chip-related stocks posted gains, including Texas Instruments, which rose 2 to 57-1/8, Micron, up 7/8 to 32-3/8, Atmel, up 1-5/8 to 34-1/8, and Applied Materials, up 1-1/4 to 29-1/4.
Among individual stocks, Tellabs soared 6 to 79 after posting strong third-quarter earnings.

U.S. Surgical added 2-1/8 to 45-3/4 on news that it was introducing the first set of instruments for minimally invasive coronary bypass graft surgery and the chairman's forecast that 1997 sales would accelerate.
Marvel Entertainment Group Inc. slid 2-3/8 to 5-5/8 on the company's warning that it would report a loss for the third quarter.
Lason Holdings, which offers outsourcing services, rose 2-3/4 to 19-3/4 in its Wall Street debut.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks fell 3.90 points to 696.74. The American Stock Exchange index was off 1.91 to 580.10.
The NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks fell 2.16 to 371.35. The average share was down 23 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was 6,832.639 down 36.280, or 0.53 percent.
